references.text: God comes to Abimelech in a dream and warns him that he will die because of the woman he has taken, for she is married. This is a direct parallel to God's intervention to protect Sarah.
Abraham prays for Abimelech, and God heals him and his household, which God had closed up on account of Sarah. A direct parallel where God afflicts a household because of Sarah.
Abimelech rebukes Isaac for lying about Rebekah and orders that no one should touch them, a parallel situation where God protects the patriarch's wife.

He allowed no one to oppress them and rebuked kings on their behalf: 'Do not touch my anointed ones; do my prophets no harm.' A direct reference to God's protection of Abraham and Sarah among the kings.
An angel of the Lord strikes Herod because he does not give glory to God, an example of God's willingness to strike those who act against his plan.
The Lord sent an angel who struck the people with a plague, an example of God's direct punishment through plagues.
A repeated pattern where God punishes a ruler's household to protect Sarai/Sarah and preserve the covenant promise.
